title: A small PHP app for teaching the web

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How much of a web framework do you actually need to build a login system? TCH099 answers with two files doing the routing and a handful of scripts doing the work.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No framework at all? What is TCH099, exactly?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's a small PHP web application built as a demo to deploy on Azure. It serves a few HTML pages, a JSON API for sign-up, login, logout and user details, and an admin page that lists every account. An Android app talks to the same API.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Students starting a team project. It has its own documentation site, written in French, with user stories, the API reference, a primer on the browser's developer tools, the Android setup and the Azure deployment steps.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How does that hand-written router work?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One file lists every route as a simple call, like get login or post api login. When a request arrives, the router checks the method, splits the address into segments, and the first route that matches runs its page or script, then stops. A segment starting with a dollar sign captures a value from the address.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Send a hello-world request with a language code in the address, and the code is captured as a variable. Send the code es and the answer comes back as Hola Mundo with the person's name. It's a neat way to see routing without any magic.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The login script checks the username against the database, verifies the password hash, and stores the user's details in the session. There are two roles, admin and client, and the admin page shows a forbidden page to clients. Passwords are hashed and every query uses prepared statements.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the Android app stays logged in?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, because it keeps one HTTP client with a cookie jar, so the session cookie from PHP survives between calls.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How does it get to Azure?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Every push to the main branch triggers a GitHub Actions workflow that zips the PHP app and deploys it to an Azure Web App. A second workflow publishes the documentation to GitHub Pages. The full write-up has the diagrams for the router and the login flow.
